title: D3 §9 patterns and the D8 §5.3 trace questions on the v1 rows
question: Do D3 §9's query patterns and the D8 §5.3 trace questions return what they should on the v1 rows, and with which plans?
method: D3 §9 texts read from code/s6_queries_d3.sql; D8 §5.3 as SQL sketches over them; rows mapped back to v1 local refs and trace C-refs; median of 7 client timings and EXPLAIN ANALYZE plans on run 1. PostgreSQL 18.6 (Ubuntu 18.6-1.pgdg24.04+2), pg_textsearch 1.5.1, vector 0.8.7, on the project-local cluster (just db-up; socket build/pg/run, port 5440, pg_textsearch preloaded); DDL applied and rows written as the NOLOGIN non-superuser cs_s6_app (SET ROLE) in cs_spike_s6 cloned from cs_template; psycopg 3.3.6 (binary), pgvector-python 0.5.1, spike venv checked against the lock (`uv sync --locked --check`: no changes) before the final run; free disk 109G at start, 106G at end.

agents.separation: coordinator brief; wrote only code/s6_*, code/s6*.py/.sql, results/s6/, records/s6.*

results.name: d8_questions_missing_expected_rows
results.note: all six questions return every expected trace claim

results.name: family_profile_normal_d3_pattern_rows
results.note: T2's answer lives on FamilyParameter entities whose identity names the family; D3 §9 needs that branch

results.name: evidence_unit_id_null
results.note: seg.attrs->>'id' reads the span's smallest segment (sentence); needs an ancestor lookup

results.name: statement_by_unit_locator_reaches_lead_in
results.note: T1's C1 sits in the lead-in paragraph outside #dfn1

conclusion: Every D3 §9 pattern returns its rows in under 2 ms on the trace data, and every D8 §5.3 question returns all its expected trace claims (extra rows come from other core units and the derived D1). Corrections for the design owner: family_profile needs the FamilyParameter branch, the evidence query's unit_id needs an ancestor lookup, and statement(page#unit) cannot reach a lead-in assumption.
